2026 Election Dates
  • March 3, 2026 - Town Voting Day
  • If you would like to request and absentee ballot, you can call the Town Clerk at 802-442-1043, email townclerk@bennintonvt.org, or you can request it online by logging in at https://mvp.vermont.gov
  • Tuesday August 11, 2026- August Primary 
  • Tuesday November 3, 2026 - General Election

HOW TO VOTE:

2026 General Election
2026 General Election is upon us, November 3, 2026.

Starting September 21, 2026, the Elections Division for the State of Vermont will start mailing out absentee ballots. Every active, registered voter in Vermont will get a ballot pursuant to state law (17 V.S.A. § 2537a) 

If you choose not to use your early ballot, remember to BYOB, bring your own ballot, to the polls on November 3rd! You can return it to us by drop-box or in person. Please write, VOTING IN PERSON, then we can make sure your absentee request is taken out of the system.  PLEASE DO NOT THROW THEM AWAY.

The ballot drop box located at 205 South Street, Bennington, will be available until Monday, November 2nd at 4:30 PM for Bennington voters ONLY. If your ballot is from a nearby town, reach out to your Town Clerk to find out how to return it. If it is returned to the Bennington drop box, it will not be counted.

As always, the Clerk’s office ONLY will close at 11:30am, Monday November 2, 2026. And will re-open regular business on Wednesday November 4, 2026. 

November 3rd, 2026, you will vote at your polling place. 7am-7pm.  For Bennington residents, vote at the Bennington Firehouse at 130 River Street. For North Bennington residents, vote at the Old Train Depot at #2 Depot Street in North Bennington.

Your voting district may have changed. To view the current district map and sample ballots, please visit: https://benningtonvt.org/services/town_clerk/elections___voter_information/index.php

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to the Clerk’s office. 
townclerk@benningtonvt.org or 802-442-1043

Learn more about Town Meeting and Voting Day on our Town Meeting page.

General Election: Mail-in Ballots

Due to passage of new laws by the Vermont Legislature, early mail-in ballots are mailed to all active voters in the State of Vermont for any General Election.

Ballots will have a return envelope included in the packet, however, you can also use the drop box located at the Bennington Town Office at 205 South Street, Bennington, VT.

If you do not wish to cast your ballot this way, please DO NOT simply dispose of your ballot.  You can return it to the Town Clerk’s Office in person or via the drop box and indicate on the envelope that you wish to vote in person on Election Day.  We will remove the request for early ballot from your voter profile.  

Another option is to BYOB (Bring Your Own Ballot) to the polls on November 5th.  If you choose this method, you can proceed to your appropriate check-in table where you will be checked-in.  The poll worker will take any mailing materials from you and let you continue to the voting booths and machine. 

What Do I Need To Do If I Moved Recently?

You can register or transfer your registration to vote, by logging into mvp.vermont.gov with your name, date of birth and Vermont driver’s license number.  When you access your profile, you will have the option to change your address.  Once completed, it will appear on the dashboard of the Town Clerk where you now reside, and they can complete the process.  If you aren’t comfortable with logging in online, you can always come into the Town Clerk’s Office and fill out a voter registration form.  Please bring your Vermont ID, as we will need the 8-digit number. 
 
What Voting District Am I In?
This map allows you to search on a given address and will place a pin on the map and tell you what district that address is in. You can also click on a given parcel on the map, and it will display the address and the district. NOTE: The link does not work on older versions of Safari web browsers; use a different web browser if you are having trouble viewing the map.  CLICK TO VIEW MAP 

TIPS ON USING THE MAP:

  • You will be leaving the town website to view the map.
  • You can enter your address, OR;
  • To navigate the map, you can click and drag to where you live.
  • You can use the scroll wheel to zoom in or out, or use the +/- buttons on the right side of the window. 
  • Click where your house is located to view what district you are in
Voter information from the VT Secretary of State (video)


When is the Next Election for Select Board and School Boards?

The next elections for Select Board and School Boards will be at our annual Town Meeting Day and Town Voting Day.  Town Meeting is the night before Town Voting Day, which is always the first Tuesday in March. The deadline for filing petitions and paperwork to be on the ballot varies depending on when Town Meeting falls. Contact the Town Clerk for each years deadline. For more information on running for the Select Board or School boards, click here.

Election Security

The VT Secretary of State has provided this video about Election security: https://youtu.be/E2TKdTs0o6I

Public Statement regarding Early Voting:

Early Absentee ballots will be automatically mailed to all active voters on the checklist for General Elections only. The mailing is completed by the Vermont Secretary of State usually later in September of even numbered years. If you wish to receive early absentee ballots for local elections or the State Primary, they must be requested by contacting the Town Clerk’s Office. This can be done on an annual basis, as we cannot maintain a permanent list. If you receive an early absentee ballot and do not wish to use it, you are not required to do so. Please indicate on the envelope “No, thank you”, “voting in person” or something similar and return it to the Clerk’s Office or deposit it in the drop box at the Town Office, your early ballot request will be removed from your voting record.

Additionally, frequently, there are social media reports of attempts to vote twice, once via early ballot and once in person. Rest assured, there are security measures in place to prevent these situations. If you vote via early ballot, your name will already be marked off the entrance checklist on Election Day. You will not be able to cast a second ballot. Please do not rely on social media for advice or so-called facts and procedures of Elections. Pursuant to 17 V.S.A. 1971 “A legal voter who knowingly casts more than one ballot at any one time of balloting for the same office shall be fined not more than $1,000.00 if the offense is committed at a primary or general election.” I encourage you to contact this office with any questions regarding elections and early voting.

Read about election information and misinformation in this article on the Vermont Secretary of State website (CLICK HERE)
